actor: platform product lead at a hyperscaler agent-platform group
job: Building a meta-harness whose headline feature enforces cost budgets, permissions, sandboxing and audit uniformly across two or more rival agent runtimes rather than only the vendor's own agents.
outcome: A second independent hyperscaler ships an agent meta-harness that brokers and constrains rival agent runtimes from one vendor-neutral policy layer.
motivation: Owning the layer above competitors' agent runtimes captures the enterprise governance control point and the consumption that flows through it.

task.who: the agent-platform group's harness and policy-engine product team
task.what: ship cross-runtime policy enforcement above rival agents
task.where: the hyperscaler's agent control plane and management console
task.why: capture the cross-vendor governance control point before rivals
task.how: a meta-harness layer wrapping multiple agent runtimes with shared policy

actor: enterprise-agent governance framework author at a standards body or analyst firm
job: Drafting an enterprise-agent governance framework that names the meta-harness layer as the prescribed point where budgets, permissions, sandboxing and audit are enforced across heterogeneous agent runtimes.
outcome: A recognized governance framework codifies the meta-harness as the prescribed cross-vendor agent policy-enforcement tier.
motivation: Codifying the control point lets the framework shape how enterprises buy and audit agents, cementing the authoring body's authority.

task.who: the framework's controls-authoring and reference-architecture working group
task.what: name the meta-harness as the prescribed policy point
task.where: the published governance framework and reference architecture
task.why: make the meta-harness the audited control point enterprises adopt
task.how: control mappings citing meta-harness budget, permission and sandbox enforcement

actor: enterprise security architect standardizing on a cross-vendor agent control plane
job: Demanding and piloting a single vendor-neutral layer that observes and constrains Claude Code, Codex and rival agent SDKs under one policy set instead of per-runtime configuration scattered across each vendor.
outcome: Enterprise buying pressure pulls a meta-harness with cross-runtime guardrails into production, validating the architectural tier.
motivation: Consolidating budgets, permissions and audit into one plane cuts governance sprawl and shrinks the attack surface of ungoverned agents.

task.who: the enterprise platform-security and agent-governance team
task.what: pilot a meta-harness enforcing one policy set across runtimes
task.where: the company's internal agent platform and security review
task.why: replace scattered per-runtime config with one auditable plane
task.how: a meta-harness brokering rival runtimes with unified budgets and sandboxing
